topic: The estimate that takes four days has already lost, regardless of the number.

slides.subtitle: (they needed it Tuesday)
slides.scene: A worn paper notebook lying open on a truck dashboard with completely blank pages, a stub of pencil resting in the fold, low afternoon sun coming through the windscreen. All vehicles and buildings in shot have COMPLETELY BLANK panels and surfaces with absolutely no writing, no company name, no logo, no lettering, no phone number and no graphics of any kind. No signage anywhere in the scene. There is NO text, no words and no labels anywhere in the image.

caption:
You measured up on Monday. They got the number on Friday.

Nothing went wrong. You were on jobs all week, and quoting is what happens after the work, which means it happens at nine at night or not at all.

But sit in their chair. They have a problem, they had three people out, and one of them came back the same afternoon. By Wednesday they are not weighing options any more, they are just waiting for you out of politeness.

The quote you send on Friday is not competing with the other quotes. It is competing with a decision that was made on Tuesday.

This is the most expensive habit in the trade and it does not look like a problem, because the work still comes in. You never see the jobs you lost this way. They just quietly go somewhere else.

Comment QUOTE and I will send the breakdown.
